comparator.sourceNotes: CurrentBLP180:81compulsory common+3conditional mathematics+6restricted policy/GIS+6restricted geography=96common;42taught LandscapeArchitecture+12thesis=54specialisation;30open. Example is for a VWO MathematicsA entrant, taking MAT14803 before MAT15103; MathematicsB entrants take MAT15303 instead. First-listed AEP22306 andGEO23306 selected from unrestricted6ECmenus, not invented compulsory packages. Complete all138prescribed taught credits, includingYRM21306 andLAR28306, before thesis; exceeds102/allB1entry and satisfies assumed specialisation preparation. General/lab/field safety zero-credit. Optional24ECinternship omitted from30open credits; no need to resolve its group-metadata maximum18against module24 for this no-internship pathway.

components.name: Landscape Perspectives
components.note: General, laboratory and fieldwork safety are additional zero-credit requirements. Complete the appropriate safety preparation before field activities and studios.

components.name: Theory and Methodology of Planning and Design
Research Methodology for Human Environment Interactions
History of Ideas in Landscape Architecture and Planning
components.note: Includes compulsory multi-day excursions, connecting landscape and planning traditions with observations and discussion on location.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.note: This example is for a student with VWO Mathematics A, taking Mathematics Applied: Introduction before Mathematics Applied: Analysis. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.

components.name: Landscape Economics and Politics
components.note: Six-credit restricted choice: Landscape Economics and Politics is selected here; Geo-Information Tools for Landscape Analysis is the other option.

components.name: Cultural and Historical Geography
components.note: Six-credit restricted choice: Cultural and Historical Geography is selected here; Environmental Psychology is the other option.

components.name: Studio Site Design
components.note: Design studio with compulsory excursions, analysis of a real site and alternative proposals at multiple scales. Fieldwork safety is required; foreign excursions require the stated travel and health-insurance preparation.

components.name: Concepts and Approaches in Landscape Architecture
Studio Regional Design
components.note: Required 9-credit regional design studio, using evidence-based design and alternative proposals at regional and detailed scales.

components.name: BSc Thesis Landscape Architecture
components.note: Required 12-credit research-based landscape design thesis: formulate a proposal and develop designs at different scales. Entry requires 102 compulsory/restricted credits including all first-year courses, Research Methodology for Human Environment Interactions and Studio Urban Design. This example completes all prescribed taught study first.

components.name: Open electives
components.note: Thirty open credits remain for a minor and/or individual electives. An internship is optional for Landscape Architecture and requires consultation with the study adviser; no internship is selected here.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target has two equally formal 54-EC specialisations, Landscape Architecture and Spatial Planning. Neither is identified as the general route, so the first current handbook specialisation is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: The explicitly supplied candidate direction is “Landscape ecology & spatial investigation”; its interest-row basis and disposition remain explicit in interestSelection.
candidateAssessments.assessment: The academic decision includes this candidate as ucr-2.

candidateAssessments.assessment: The academic decision includes this candidate as ucr-3.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest response materially addresses landscape processes, geospatial evidence and nature-based interventions, with human, economic and visual evaluation. A second response prioritises ecological mechanisms and quantitative environmental evidence; only after accepting it is a third response accepted with socio-legal, governance and participation priorities. All are coherent, feasible and substantively distinct. Professional landscape design, planting/construction representation and repeated studios remain major gaps. Stop at the three-alternative maximum without presenting any UCR route as equivalent professional landscape-architecture training.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Shared elementary differentiation/integration and dynamic models; WUR dedicates its course to calculus and differential equations, while UCR embeds these tools in physical/environmental science.
Shared geological and geomorphological processes forming landscapes; WUR integrates Dutch hydrology, soils, land use, vegetation and historical landscape identity more broadly.
Shared soils, groundwater and land-use constraints; WUR includes its own geology/soil-landscape field excursion.
Shared ecological principles, ecosystem processes and interactions; WUR provides a compact introductory ecology foundation.

Shared applied investigation of a concrete environmental/place issue, stakeholder interests and proposed intervention advice; WUR additionally produces a spatial/action plan through an intensive field-based planning studio.
Shared analysis of place and nature-based intervention proposals; WUR provides a full landscape studio with a client brief, multiple scales and professional representational practice.
Shared public goods, externalities, economic policy and distribution; WUR specifically applies economics and politics to land use, locations and landscape value.
Shared understanding of water movement, quality and environmental relationships; UCR emphasises delta risks and adaptation rather than a global introductory hydrology survey.
Shared visual evaluation of space, form, colour and composition through art; WUR adds philosophical/environmental aesthetic frameworks and critique of landscape designs.
Shared investigation of land, cultural identity, historical power and contemporary uses; UCR provides an Indigenous North American case, not WUR’s broad cultural/historical landscape geography.
Shared research design, questions, qualitative data collection, observation and interviews; WUR develops a broader human-environment research proposal across study designs.
Shared estimation, testing and regression as foundations for empirical research.
Shared GIS, spatial data handling, cartography, terrain/surface analysis and remote-sensing methods with practical projects.
Shared science-informed practical investigation of spatial/environmental problems and intervention projects; WUR teaches integrated creative landscape planning/design beyond geospatial engineering.

notes.text: WUR combines landscape processes with repeated site, urban and regional design studios, planting, construction, representation, aesthetics and a research-based design thesis. UCR can address landscapes through substantial environmental and geospatial investigation, nature-based interventions, visual analysis and governance. The professional studio sequence, planting/construction detailing and design-thesis training remain major differences.

audience.programmeDescription: Landscape Architecture and Planning studies how people shape places for human and ecological needs. This Dutch-taught programme combines soil, water, ecology, geography and spatial evidence with planning and creative design. The example follows the Landscape Architecture specialisation.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes respond through landscape processes and nature-based interventions, ecological and spatial investigation, or land-use governance and participation. WUR offers much more sustained landscape design, studio practice, planting, construction and representation. UCR’s Spatial Planning course supports geospatial environmental applications; it does not replace that professional training.

curriculum.limitation: This 180-credit example contains 96 common credits, 42 taught specialisation credits, a 12-credit design thesis and 30 open credits. It assumes VWO Mathematics A preparation and completes the required taught study and safety preparation before the thesis.
